title: Remove Outermost Parentheses
summary: A valid parentheses string is either empty, starts and ends with a pair of parentheses with content in between, or a concatenation of two valid parentheses strings.
statement: A valid parentheses string is either empty, starts and ends with a pair of parentheses with content in between, or a concatenation of two valid parentheses strings. For instance, '', '()', '(())()', and '(()(()))' are valid. A string is primitive if it cannot be split into two nonempty valid strings. Given a valid string, decompose it into primitives and remove the outermost parentheses of each primitive.
constraints: s is a nonempty valid parentheses string.
Remove the first and last character of each primitive component.
hints: Outermost parentheses are precisely those crossing depth zero and one.
Track nesting depth during one scan.
Increment before deciding to keep an opening; decide before decrementing a closing.
All characters at internal depth remain, while each primitive boundary is omitted.
editorial: All characters at internal depth remain, while each primitive boundary is omitted.

tests.explanation: The primitives (()()) and (()) become ()() and (), concatenated as ()()().
Each primitive is (), so removing both outer characters leaves empty text.
